body:
An additional control with level 3 should be added to [11.6](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x20-V11-Cryptography.md#v116-public-key-cryptography) to address forward secrecy.

Control
Verify that forward secrecy is ensured using appropriate algorithms and protocols.
Level = 3

Reasoning
Forward secrecy is essential for high risk applications. Depending on the protocol and algorithms used, forward secrecy requires different measures.

I don't think we would want to include forward secrecy in "V11.6 Public Key Cryptography" because there are legitimate cases of public key cryptography which don't use forward secrecy. For example, non-interactive public-key encryption (as used for Encrypted Client Hello and other usages of HPKE) is typically not forward secret.

The problem I see here is, that 12.1.2 is only about TLS. Forward secrecy is a general security measure for cryptography. TLS is just one of many applications.

Notice: While we can require forward secrecy for TLS, it can only be a recommendation for asymmetric cryptography in general.

> The problem I see here is, that 12.1.2 is only about TLS. Forward secrecy is a general security measure for cryptography. TLS is just one of many applications.
>
> Notice: While we can require forward secrecy for TLS, it can only be a recommendation for asymmetric cryptography in general.

Yes, we cannot require forward secrecy everywhere encryption is used.

Some examples which are relevant in the context of web applications:

* Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) does not provide forward secrecy. It relies on a non-ephemeral server private key.
* Encrypted token such as encrypted JWTs (or other JWEs) do not provide forward secrecy. The rely on non-ephemeral audience private keys.

This would leave us to something like "verify  forward secrecy is used whenever it makes sense to use it" which does not constitute a very good requirement. 😄 (it might be a recommendation)
